uslaw-usc-t2-s190d:
Section 190d of Title 2 of the United States Code charges the standing committees of Congress with continuing review of the laws. Oversight, not just lawmaking, is the subject here. The section explains why that review duty exists before it assigns it.

Congress needs help in judging how its laws work in practice. Committees are to analyse, appraise, and evaluate the application of the laws. They watch over how the laws are administered and executed by others. The same study feeds the making of new law. Committees use it to frame changes in existing laws and to shape added legislation where needed. Each standing committee of the Senate and the House carries the duty. The review covers the laws, or parts of laws, within its subject field. The section is the statutory root of routine congressional oversight.
